evidence.description: The workflow collapses the nightly rows to exactly one mean syllable rate per bird before any test runs, so each independent unit (bird_id) enters the downstream procedure once.
evidence.observed_value: summarise_birds returns one (bird, diet, nights, mean) tuple per unique bird_id

source_refs.quoted_text:
def summarise_birds(session_rows: List[Dict[str, str]]) -> List[BirdSummary]:
    """Collapse the nightly rows to one mean syllable rate per bird."""

rates.setdefault(bird, []).append(float(row[VALUE_COLUMN]))
    order = sorted(rates, key=lambda bird: (diet[bird], bird))
    return [(b, diet[b], len(rates[b]), fmean(rates[b])) for b in order]

evidence.observed_value: treated/control lists of length 6 each are built from per-bird summaries and passed to mannwhitneyu

evidence.description: The reported statistics are numerically consistent only with a 6-vs-6 bird-level test: U = 35 is bounded by the 6x6 maximum of 36 (a 24-vs-24 row-level test would allow U up to 576), rank-biserial 0.944 = 2*35/36 - 1, and p = 0.0043 equals 4/924, the exact two-sided tail for n1 = n2 = 6 with one crossing pair (ZF-16 mean 6.72 below ZF-03 mean 6.95). Recomputed per-bird means from data/input.csv match the report's table (e.g. ZF-01: (7.72+7.91+8.02+7.75)/4 = 7.85; ZF-03: 6.95).
evidence.observed_value: U = 35, p = 0.0043, rank-biserial = 0.944, consistent with n = 6 vs 6 bird means

U = 35, p = 0.0043, rank-biserial correlation = 0.944.

[selected-result] Supplemented birds sang faster than controls: exact two-sided Mann-Whitney U test on 12 bird-level mean syllable rates (6 supplemented, 6 control, one value per bird), U = 35, p = 0.0043, rank-biserial correlation = 0.944, median difference 1.03 syl/s.

so the independent unit is the bird (`bird_id`). Every bird is collapsed
to its mean syllable rate across its own nights before any test is run,
leaving 12 analysed values -- 6 supplemented and 6 control -- that is,
exactly one analysed value per independent unit.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to show that the 48 session rows entered the Mann-Whitney test as separate observations. Tracing the code, the only data path to stats.mannwhitneyu goes through summarise_birds, which keys on bird_id and returns fmean per bird; there is no branch that passes row-level rates. I then checked whether the reported numbers could have come from a row-level test: with 24 supplemented and 24 control rows the U statistic would range up to 576, but the report shows U = 35 with maximum 36 implied by rank-biserial 0.944 = 2*35/36 - 1, and p = 0.0043 matches the exact 6-vs-6 two-sided tail 4/924 given exactly one discordant pair among bird means (ZF-16 6.72 < ZF-03 6.95). I recomputed all 12 per-bird means from data/input.csv by hand and they match the report's per-bird table, and the group summaries (supplemented mean of means 7.34, control 6.38, median difference 1.03) follow from those means. The attempt to demonstrate repeated unit entry failed on every check.
